case.pattern_description: A coordinated multi-card micro-billing scheme involving recurring online authorizations under $10 for product C, spaced over multiple weeks without an escalating larger purchase. The scheme has expanded across 19 cards and 19 unrelated customers with contiguous transaction IDs, representing automated low-dollar card enumeration or systematic merchant draining rather than standard card testing. Because this coordinated cross-customer abuse does not fit established typologies, it is classified as undocumented under Rule R9.

evidence.claim: Customer reported: Customer C00348 message: 'I did not make these charges on my card. Please look into it.' Refers to 3660250.

Card C00348-K1 made 6 online product-C charges totalling $23.17 over 21.2 days (3660245, 3660246, 3660247, 3660248, 3660249, 3660250); in its 29 transactions of the 60 days before, that kind made up 0%. Every one is a tiny authorisation, spread over days with no larger purchase after them, so they are not R5's sequence of three within an hour followed by a purchase.

19 other cards (19 other customers) newly show the same signature in the 30 days to the alert - 3+ online authorisations under $10, on a card that had not made such charges before - against 7 and 4 in the same window one and two months earlier: C05083-K1, C12975-K2, C00129-K1, C01326-K2, C04528-K1, C09471-K2, C13290-K1, C03611-K2, C04105-K2, C05263-K2, C06198-K1, C08972-K1.

evidence.claim: Flagged transaction 3660250 is the culmination of an anomalous run of 6 consecutive low-value online authorizations under $10 (ranging from $2.10 to $5.08, totaling $23.17) between 2017-01-07 and 2017-01-28 for product C, spanning sequential IDs 3660245 through 3660250.

Scheme peer analysis identifies 19 other cards across 19 customers exhibiting the identical anomalous signature of 3+ online authorizations under $10 on cards without prior such charges, with scheme volume growing from 4 cards two months ago to 19 currently, sharing sequential transaction IDs in the 3660xxx block.

evidence.claim: The flagged transaction 3660250 represents product C online, which is completely new for the holder whose prior baseline consists of in-person product W transactions (such as transaction 3601214 for $139.34), with no matching recurring pattern.

Closed case CC-3841 on card C01099-K1 confirmed fraudulent activity under an undocumented pattern involving structured online authorizations designed to stay under threshold amounts without matching standard typologies.

evidence.claim: Billing region 264 of the flagged transaction 3660250 represents 36.2% of the card's historical activity (54 of 149 prior transactions), showing that the card has regular legitimate usage in this region.
The flagged transaction 3660250 and associated run transactions were conducted without a device ID, exhibiting no proxy flag, and card C00348-K1 has no suspicious device ring membership (ring_id -1).

The alert text also contained 2 segment(s) addressed to the system rather than an analyst (outcome_directive, override, role_marker). They were set aside and used neither as evidence nor as instruction; the decision rests on the evidence above.

evidence.claim: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns: Rule R9: Undocumented patterns. When activity fits none of the known patterns but the evidence shows coordinated or repeated abuse across customers, recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `FILE_REPORT`, and `ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST`, and describe the pattern in your own words. Do not force it into a known category.

case.summary: Customer C00348 alerted the bank to unauthorized activity on card C00348-K1 regarding transaction 3660250 ($4.05). Graph investigation revealed a 6-transaction run of low-value online product C authorizations between January 7 and January 28, 2017, totaling $23.17, which is completely unprecedented against the cardholder's historical baseline of in-person product W purchases. Crucially, scheme peer analysis identified 19 other cards across 19 customers exhibiting identical micro-billing patterns with contiguous transaction IDs in the 3660xxx block, reflecting coordinated batch processing. Based on the customer dispute and decisive cross-card evidence, the activity was confirmed fraudulent and classified as an undocumented scheme under Rule R9. The card was blocked, peer cards were flagged for monitoring, and a suspicious activity report was initiated.

sar.narrative: This suspicious activity report details a coordinated micro-billing fraud scheme affecting card C00348-K1 belonging to customer C00348, alongside 19 peer cards across 19 unrelated customer accounts including C05083-K1, C12975-K2, and C06198-K1. Between January 7, 2017, and January 28, 2017, six consecutive online authorizations totaling $23.17 were posted to card C00348-K1 for product C, with individual amounts ranging from $2.10 to $5.08. The transactions were initiated via the online channel across billing regions 325 and 264, without captured device IDs or proxy records. On January 28, 2017, customer C00348 formally disputed transaction 3660250, stating that they did not authorize the charges. Internal investigation confirmed that online product C purchases were entirely inconsistent with the cardholder's baseline, which historically consisted of in-person product W transactions. The disputed charge formed part of an unbroken sequence of transactions (IDs 3660245 through 3660250) indicating automated batch processing. Graph analysis demonstrated that 19 peer cards exhibited the identical signature of three or more new online authorizations under $10, sharing clustered transaction IDs within the 3660xxx block. The overall scheme exhibited coordinated multi-card growth, escalating from 4 cards two months prior to 19 cards in the current window. Because the transactions occurred over several weeks without an escalating larger purchase, the pattern reflects systematic low-dollar merchant exploitation rather than conventional card testing. Total fraudulent exposure on card C00348-K1 is $23.17, prompting the institution to block the card and initiate ongoing monitoring on all connected accounts.

stop_reason: The investigation stopped pursuant to policy section 6 because the fraud probability reached a decisive 0.95 based on multiple independent lines of incriminating evidence, including the customer dispute, unprecedented product C purchasing patterns, and cross-card links to an escalating 19-card batch-processing scheme. Further investigative steps would not change the outcome or action plan.
